title: Genesis Chapter 37 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Genesis chapter 37 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Genesis Chapter 37 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Genesis Chapter 37.

questions.question: Where did Jacob dwell according to Genesis 37?
questions.correctAnswer: Land of Canaan
questions.explanation: Genesis 37:1 states that Jacob dwelt in the land of Canaan, where his father was a stranger.

questions.question: How old was Joseph when he was feeding the flock with his brethren?
questions.correctAnswer: Seventeen years old
questions.explanation: Genesis 37:2 specifies that Joseph was seventeen years old when he was feeding the flock with his brethren.

questions.question: Who did Joseph bring an evil report about to his father?
questions.correctAnswer: His brethren
questions.explanation: Genesis 37:2 describes that Joseph brought an evil report about his brethren to his father.

questions.question: Why did Israel love Joseph more than all his children?
options: Because he was the son of his old age
Because he was a great shepherd
Because he was a good hunter
questions.correctAnswer: Because he was the son of his old age
questions.explanation: Genesis 37:3 explains that Israel loved Joseph more because he was the son of his old age.

questions.question: What special garment did Jacob make for Joseph?
questions.correctAnswer: A coat of many colours
questions.explanation: Genesis 37:3 states that Jacob made Joseph a coat of many colours.

questions.question: How did Joseph's brethren feel when they saw their father loved Joseph more?
questions.correctAnswer: They hated him
questions.explanation: Genesis 37:4 says that Joseph's brethren hated him when they saw their father loved him more than them.

questions.question: True or False: Joseph told his brethren about a dream and they liked it.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Genesis 37:5 indicates that Joseph told his brethren a dream and they hated him yet more.

questions.question: What did Joseph's first dream involve?
options: Sheaves in the field bowing to his sheaf
The sun, moon, and stars bowing
questions.correctAnswer: Sheaves in the field bowing to his sheaf
questions.explanation: Genesis 37:7 describes Joseph's first dream about sheaves in the field bowing to his sheaf.

questions.question: What question did Joseph's brethren ask him because of his dream?
options: Shalt thou indeed reign over us?
Do you want to be a shepherd?
questions.correctAnswer: Shalt thou indeed reign over us?
questions.explanation: Genesis 37:8 shows that his brethren asked if Joseph would reign over them because of his dream.

questions.question: True or False: Joseph had a second dream involving the sun, moon, and eleven stars making obeisance to him.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Genesis 37:9 confirms Joseph dreamed about the sun, moon, and eleven stars bowing to him.

questions.question: How did Jacob react when Joseph told him the second dream?
questions.correctAnswer: He rebuked him
questions.explanation: Genesis 37:10 states Jacob rebuked Joseph after hearing the dream.

questions.question: What did Joseph's brethren do after envying him, according to Genesis 37?
options: Went to feed their father's flock in Shechem
questions.correctAnswer: Went to feed their father's flock in Shechem
questions.explanation: Genesis 37:12 says his brethren went to feed their father's flock in Shechem.

questions.question: True or False: Joseph immediately refused to go to his brethren when his father asked him.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Genesis 37:13 shows Joseph responded 'Here am I' when his father asked him to go to his brethren.

questions.question: In Genesis 37, which event comes first?
options: Joseph's coat is dipped in blood
Joseph goes to find his brethren in Shechem
questions.correctAnswer: Joseph dreams about sheaves
questions.explanation: Joseph's dream about sheaves occurs first (Genesis 37:5-7) before he goes to find his brethren or is sold (later verses).

questions.question: What did Joseph's father do when he saw the coat dipped in blood?
questions.correctAnswer: Rent his clothes and mourned
questions.explanation: Genesis 37:34 describes Jacob tearing his clothes and mourning upon seeing Joseph's coat dipped in blood.

medium.title: Genesis Chapter 37 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Genesis Chapter 37 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What task did Jacob send Joseph to do in Genesis 37:13-14?
options: See whether it be well with his brethren and the flocks
Find a new place to settle
Build a shelter for the flocks
questions.correctAnswer: See whether it be well with his brethren and the flocks
questions.explanation: Genesis 37:13-14 shows Jacob instructing Joseph to check on his brothers and the welfare of the flocks, demonstrating trust and responsibility.

questions.question: Who found Joseph wandering in the field according to Genesis 37:15?
questions.correctAnswer: A certain man
questions.explanation: Genesis 37:15 mentions that a certain man found Joseph wandering and asked him what he sought, highlighting Joseph's search for his brothers.

questions.question: What did Joseph say he was seeking when asked by the man in Genesis 37:16?
questions.correctAnswer: His brethren
questions.explanation: Genesis 37:16 records Joseph's response that he was seeking his brethren and wanted to know where they fed their flocks, showing his concern for them.

questions.question: Where did the man say Joseph's brethren had gone in Genesis 37:17?
questions.correctAnswer: To Dothan
questions.explanation: Genesis 37:17 states the brethren had departed to Dothan, and Joseph followed them there, demonstrating obedience to his father's command.

questions.question: What was the brothers' plan when they saw Joseph coming in Genesis 37:18-20?
options: To kill him and hide the body
To ask him to return home
questions.correctAnswer: To kill him and hide the body
questions.explanation: Genesis 37:18-20 reveals the brothers conspired to kill Joseph and conceal it by saying an evil beast devoured him, showing their hatred fueled by jealousy.

questions.question: How did Reuben intervene in the brothers' plot against Joseph according to Genesis 37:21-22?
options: He convinced them to free Joseph immediately
He suggested casting Joseph into a pit without shedding blood
He planned to kill Joseph himself
He told their father about the plot
questions.correctAnswer: He suggested casting Joseph into a pit without shedding blood
questions.explanation: Genesis 37:21-22 shows Reuben persuading the brothers not to kill Joseph but to put him in a pit, intending to rescue him later and return him to their father.

questions.question: What did the brothers do to Joseph's coat when he arrived according to Genesis 37:23?
options: They gifted it back to him
They gave it to their father
questions.correctAnswer: They stripped it off him
questions.explanation: Genesis 37:23 indicates the brothers stripped Joseph of his coat of many colours, symbolizing their rejection and jealousy towards him.

questions.question: What was the condition of the pit into which Joseph was cast as described in Genesis 37:24?
options: It was empty with no water
questions.correctAnswer: It was empty with no water
questions.explanation: Genesis 37:24 states the pit was empty and had no water, which meant Joseph was trapped but not drowned, aligning with Reuben's plan to rescue him.

questions.question: What happened while the brothers were eating bread after casting Joseph into the pit according to Genesis 37:25?
options: A group of Midianites passed by
A company of Ishmeelites came from Gilead
Jacob arrived to search for Joseph
questions.correctAnswer: A company of Ishmeelites came from Gilead
questions.explanation: Genesis 37:25 describes Ishmeelites coming with camels carrying spices, which sets the stage for Joseph's later sale to Egypt.

questions.question: What alternative plan did Judah propose instead of killing Joseph as per Genesis 37:26-27?
options: To leave Joseph in the pit
To sell Joseph to the Ishmeelites
To send Joseph back to their father
To make Joseph a servant in their household
questions.correctAnswer: To sell Joseph to the Ishmeelites
questions.explanation: Genesis 37:26-27 records Judah suggesting selling Joseph to avoid killing him, showing a measure of mercy and practical thinking among the brothers.

questions.question: What did the brothers do with Joseph after selling him according to Genesis 37:28?
options: They told their father the truth
They sold him for twenty pieces of silver and brought him into Egypt
questions.correctAnswer: They sold him for twenty pieces of silver and brought him into Egypt
questions.explanation: Genesis 37:28 states Joseph was sold for twenty pieces of silver to the Ishmeelites and taken to Egypt, initiating his journey far from home.

questions.question: What was Reuben's reaction when he found the pit empty in Genesis 37:29?
questions.correctAnswer: He rent his clothes
questions.explanation: Genesis 37:29 shows Reuben tearing his clothes in grief and distress upon realizing Joseph was no longer in the pit, revealing his sorrow and guilt.

questions.question: What did the brothers do with Joseph's coat to deceive their father according to Genesis 37:31-32?
options: They dipped it in goat's blood and presented it to Jacob
They hid it in the field
questions.correctAnswer: They dipped it in goat's blood and presented it to Jacob
questions.explanation: Genesis 37:31-32 describes the brothers killing a goat and using its blood to stain Joseph's coat to falsely convince their father Joseph was killed by a wild beast.

questions.question: How did Jacob react when he saw Joseph's bloodied coat as described in Genesis 37:33-34?
options: He rent his clothes and mourned many days
questions.correctAnswer: He rent his clothes and mourned many days
questions.explanation: Genesis 37:33-34 shows Jacob mourning deeply for Joseph, tearing his clothes and putting on sackcloth, reflecting his grief and despair.

questions.question: Based on Genesis 37:13-22, how does this passage teach about obedience and trust in God's plan despite hardships?
options: Joseph disobeyed his father and got lost
Joseph obeyed his father by seeking his brothers even though it led to danger
The brothers trusted God to protect Joseph
Jacob sent Joseph to Egypt intentionally
questions.correctAnswer: Joseph obeyed his father by seeking his brothers even though it led to danger
questions.explanation: Genesis 37:13-22 shows Joseph's faithful obedience to his father's command to check on his brothers, trusting God despite the brothers' hostile plans, teaching perseverance and faith.

hard.title: Genesis Chapter 37 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Genesis Chapter 37.

questions.question: What items were the Ishmeelites carrying when they passed by Joseph's brothers?
questions.correctAnswer: Spicery, balm, and myrrh
questions.explanation: Genesis 37:25 states that the Ishmeelites came bearing spicery, balm, and myrrh, going to carry it down to Egypt, showing the nature of their merchandise.

questions.question: Who proposed selling Joseph to the Ishmeelites instead of killing him?
questions.correctAnswer: Judah
questions.explanation: In Genesis 37:26-27, Judah suggests selling Joseph to avoid shedding blood, emphasizing brotherly flesh and preserving their hands from guilt.

questions.question: For how much money was Joseph sold to the Ishmeelites?
questions.correctAnswer: Twenty pieces of silver
questions.explanation: Genesis 37:28 details that Joseph was sold for twenty pieces of silver, a sum that later echoes the price for which Judas betrayed Jesus in the New Testament (Matthew 26:15).

questions.question: What did Reuben do when he discovered Joseph was no longer in the pit?
questions.correctAnswer: He rent his clothes
questions.explanation: Genesis 37:29 shows Reuben's grief by tearing his clothes, a traditional expression of mourning in ancient Near Eastern culture.

questions.question: What did Joseph's brothers do to make it appear that Joseph was killed by an animal?
options: They dipped his coat in goat's blood
questions.correctAnswer: They dipped his coat in goat's blood
questions.explanation: Genesis 37:31 describes how the brothers killed a kid of the goats and dipped Joseph's coat in its blood to deceive their father into thinking Joseph was devoured by a beast.

questions.question: How did Jacob react when he received Joseph’s bloodied coat?
questions.correctAnswer: He immediately mourned deeply
questions.explanation: Genesis 37:34-35 recounts Jacob tearing his clothes, wearing sackcloth, mourning many days, refusing comfort as he believed Joseph was dead.

questions.question: To whom was Joseph sold once the Midianites bought him?
questions.correctAnswer: Potiphar
questions.explanation: Genesis 37:36 states that the Midianites sold Joseph to Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh and captain of the guard, setting the stage for Joseph’s future in Egypt.

questions.question: What literary device is prominently used in Genesis 37 to highlight Joseph's dreams and his brothers' reactions?
questions.correctAnswer: Foreshadowing
questions.explanation: Genesis 37:5-11 uses Joseph's dreams to foreshadow his future rise and dominance over his brothers, a key narrative technique that sets up later fulfillment in Genesis 41.

questions.question: What is the Hebrew meaning of the word translated as 'coat of many colours' given to Joseph?
questions.correctAnswer: A richly ornamented coat
questions.explanation: The Hebrew term 'ketonet passim' in Genesis 37:3 likely means a long, richly ornamented robe signifying favor and status, not merely a multi-colored garment.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the theme of betrayal by a brother seen in Genesis 37?
questions.correctAnswer: Psalm 41:9
questions.explanation: Psalm 41:9 speaks of a close friend and companion who betrays the psalmist, echoing the fraternal betrayal of Joseph by his brothers in Genesis 37.

questions.question: What was the origin of the traders who bought Joseph from the Midianites?
questions.correctAnswer: Ishmeelites
questions.explanation: Genesis 37:28 specifies that Joseph was sold to the Ishmeelites, who were associated with trading caravans traveling to Egypt, reflecting ancient Near Eastern trade routes.

questions.question: What did Joseph’s father, Jacob, declare about mourning for Joseph?
options: He would mourn until he died
He would go down into the grave mourning for him
questions.correctAnswer: He would go down into the grave mourning for him
questions.explanation: Genesis 37:35 quotes Jacob saying he will go down into the grave mourning for Joseph, expressing deep, enduring grief.

questions.question: True or False: Reuben was the only brother who wanted to kill Joseph.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Genesis 37:18-20 shows that all the brothers conspired to kill Joseph, but Reuben intervened to save him by suggesting they throw him in a pit instead.

questions.question: True or False: Joseph’s dreams symbolically predicted his future rise to power over his family.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Genesis 37:5-11 records Joseph’s dreams where his sheaf and celestial bodies bow to him, symbolizing his future authority over his brothers and parents, fulfilled in Genesis 41.

questions.question: What was the reaction of Joseph’s brothers when they saw him coming from afar?
options: They asked him to join their work
questions.correctAnswer: They conspired to kill him
questions.explanation: Genesis 37:18 states that Joseph’s brothers conspired against him to slay him even before he came near, showing their hatred fueled by jealousy.

theological.title: Genesis Chapter 37 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Genesis Chapter 37 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Joseph’s coat of many colours, given by Jacob, signify in the context of Genesis 37?
options: Jacob's favoritism and the special status given to Joseph
A symbol of Joseph's role as a priest
A common garment given to all sons
questions.correctAnswer: Jacob's favoritism and the special status given to Joseph
questions.explanation: Genesis 37:3 states that Jacob loved Joseph more than all his children and made him a coat of many colours, symbolizing favoritism and a special status within the family.

questions.question: How does Genesis 37:5-8 reveal the spiritual danger of pride through Joseph’s dreams and his brothers’ reactions?
options: Joseph’s dreams reveal pride in dominion, provoking hatred from his brothers
Joseph’s dreams show humility and servanthood
His brothers rejoice in his dreams as signs of blessing
Joseph’s dreams predict immediate peace in the family
questions.correctAnswer: Joseph’s dreams reveal pride in dominion, provoking hatred from his brothers
questions.explanation: In Genesis 37:5-8, Joseph’s dreams depict his sheaf rising and others bowing to it, symbolizing dominion, which his brothers perceive as prideful, causing them to hate him.

questions.question: What theological truth about divine sovereignty and providence is demonstrated by Joseph's brothers selling him into Egypt rather than killing him outright?
options: God uses human evil actions to accomplish His redemptive plan
God abandons His people in times of trouble
Human free will is absolute and unchecked
Joseph’s brothers acted without any consequences
questions.correctAnswer: God uses human evil actions to accomplish His redemptive plan
questions.explanation: Genesis 37:27-28 shows Joseph’s brothers selling him, an evil act that God sovereignly uses to bring Joseph to Egypt, foreshadowing salvation history (compare Acts 2:23).

questions.question: Which divine attribute is demonstrated by Jacob’s observance and restraint despite his sons’ envy and hatred toward Joseph?
questions.correctAnswer: Patience and discernment
questions.explanation: Genesis 37:11 notes that Jacob observed the envying of Joseph’s brothers, showing his patience and discernment rather than immediate judgment or anger.

questions.question: In what way does Genesis 37:36 connect Joseph’s story to the broader redemptive narrative of salvation history?
options: Joseph’s sale into Egypt prefigures God’s deliverance of Israel from bondage
Joseph’s sale marks the end of Israel’s family line
It shows Egypt’s permanent control over Israel
Joseph’s story is isolated without redemptive implications
questions.correctAnswer: Joseph’s sale into Egypt prefigures God’s deliverance of Israel from bondage
questions.explanation: Genesis 37:36 tells of Joseph sold to Potiphar in Egypt, which begins the story leading to Israel’s sojourn and later deliverance, foreshadowing God's redemptive salvation (Exodus 3:7-8).

questions.question: What doctrine about human sinfulness and fraternal conflict is taught by the conspiracy of Joseph’s brothers against him in Genesis 37:18-20?
options: Human sin leads to envy, hatred, and attempts to destroy others
Human nature is inherently peaceful and loving
Sin is absent in family relationships
questions.correctAnswer: Human sin leads to envy, hatred, and attempts to destroy others
questions.explanation: Genesis 37:18-20 depicts Joseph’s brothers conspiring to kill him out of hatred fueled by envy, illustrating the destructive power of sin within relationships.

questions.question: How does the interaction between Reuben and his brothers regarding Joseph (Genesis 37:21-22) demonstrate a complex human response to sin within a fallen family?
options: Reuben seeks to rescue Joseph, showing remorse and a desire to restore
Reuben is indifferent to Joseph’s fate
All brothers unanimously agree on killing Joseph
questions.correctAnswer: Reuben seeks to rescue Joseph, showing remorse and a desire to restore
questions.explanation: Genesis 37:21-22 records Reuben intervening to save Joseph from death by suggesting to cast him into a pit instead, indicating a conflicted conscience and a desire to preserve life.

questions.question: What does the sending of Joseph to check on his brothers and the flocks (Genesis 37:13-14) reveal about Jacob’s parental role and providential arrangement?
options: Jacob’s sending Joseph sets in motion God’s providential plan despite human intentions
Jacob was unaware of his sons’ hatred
Jacob intended Joseph to dominate his brothers immediately
Jacob’s actions were impulsive and without purpose
questions.correctAnswer: Jacob’s sending Joseph sets in motion God’s providential plan despite human intentions
questions.explanation: In Genesis 37:13-14, Jacob sends Joseph to his brothers for a report, unknowingly initiating events that align with God’s sovereign plan for Joseph’s future.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that the story of Joseph’s betrayal is merely a family drama with no divine purpose. What does Genesis 37:27-28 actually teach about God’s use of evil intentions for good?
options: God providentially uses human sin to bring about His redemptive purposes
The story has no divine significance and is purely coincidental
God condones evil actions by Joseph’s brothers
The events are random and meaningless
questions.correctAnswer: God providentially uses human sin to bring about His redemptive purposes
questions.explanation: Genesis 37:27-28 records Joseph’s sale to Ishmaelites, an act of evil, yet God’s providence is evident as it leads to Joseph’s rise in Egypt, demonstrating divine sovereignty over human sin (Romans 8:28).

questions.question: What doctrinal insight about mourning and hope is revealed through Jacob’s response to Joseph’s apparent death in Genesis 37:34-35?
options: Jacob mourns deeply, showing the reality of human grief even amidst divine promises
Jacob immediately loses faith in God
Jacob rejoices prematurely thinking Joseph is safe
Jacob ignores the news and continues life as usual
questions.correctAnswer: Jacob mourns deeply, showing the reality of human grief even amidst divine promises
questions.explanation: Genesis 37:34-35 shows Jacob mourning for Joseph, reflecting human sorrow and the tension between grief and hope in God’s unfolding plan (Psalm 34:18).

questions.question: How do Joseph’s dreams in Genesis 37:5-10 foreshadow Christ’s universal kingship and the submission of creation to Him?
options: The dreams symbolize Christ’s future reign over all peoples
The dreams predict Joseph becoming a farmer
The dreams indicate Joseph’s permanent exile
The dreams show the futility of divine plans
questions.correctAnswer: The dreams symbolize Christ’s future reign over all peoples
questions.explanation: Genesis 37:5-10 depicts Joseph’s sheaf, sun, moon, and stars bowing, typologically foreshadowing Christ’s universal kingship where all creation submits (Philippians 2:9-11).

questions.question: What synthesis of Genesis 37:23-24 and 37:31-32 explains the theme of substitutionary suffering and deception in Joseph’s narrative?
options: Joseph is stripped of his coat and replaced symbolically by a goat’s blood to deceive Jacob
Joseph willingly sacrifices his coat to save his brothers
Jacob gives Joseph a new coat after the pit incident
Joseph’s brothers repent and confess immediately
questions.correctAnswer: Joseph is stripped of his coat and replaced symbolically by a goat’s blood to deceive Jacob
questions.explanation: Genesis 37:23-24 describes Joseph stripped and thrown into a pit; 37:31-32 shows his coat dipped in goat’s blood to deceive Jacob, illustrating substitutionary suffering and deceit.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is demonstrated through Jacob’s enduring grief and refusal to be comforted after believing Joseph dead (Genesis 37:34-35)?
options: God’s sovereign allowance of human suffering and emotional depth
God’s immediate intervention to prevent sorrow
questions.correctAnswer: God’s sovereign allowance of human suffering and emotional depth
questions.explanation: Genesis 37:34-35 shows Jacob’s deep mourning, indicating God’s allowance for genuine human suffering within His sovereign plan, reflecting the incarnational aspect of God’s empathy (Hebrews 4:15).

questions.question: How do Genesis 37:15-17 and 37:18-20 together illustrate the theological tension between human free will and divine providence?
options: Joseph’s seeking and his brothers’ plotting show human choices within God’s sovereign plan
Joseph is unaware of his brothers and acts without free will
His brothers are forced by God to hate Joseph
There is no divine involvement in these events
questions.correctAnswer: Joseph’s seeking and his brothers’ plotting show human choices within God’s sovereign plan
questions.explanation: Genesis 37:15-17 shows Joseph seeking his brothers, while 37:18-20 shows their conspiracy, revealing human free will operating within God’s providential framework (Proverbs 16:9).

questions.question: What doctrinal teaching about God’s justice and human responsibility is conveyed through Reuben’s plan to save Joseph but failing to prevent his sale (Genesis 37:21-29)?
options: Human efforts can be flawed, but God’s justice ultimately prevails
Human plans always succeed without failure
God condones the selling of Joseph
Reuben’s plan was perfect and fully effective
questions.correctAnswer: Human efforts can be flawed, but God’s justice ultimately prevails
questions.explanation: Genesis 37:21-29 shows Reuben’s attempt to save Joseph fails when brothers sell him, highlighting human fallibility but God’s justice and plan continue to unfold (Romans 12:19).
